comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the fix is gated to MacBook9,1 / MacBook10,1 and does nothing on other hardware. The root cause is consistent with mainline Linux 7.2 (`cs420x.c` selects the CS4208 Apple fixups only for Apple PCI subsystem IDs), and the WirePlumber rule, efivarfs immutable-flag handling and `SuspendState=freeze` drop-in are valid for current upstream sources.

**Outcome:** the main issues are in how and where the out-of-tree driver is built. On a fresh ISO install the new step fails and stops the installation on the two target models, and the "already installed" check can accept a failed or wrong-kernel build, leaving speakers silent with the migration recorded as done. The suspend explanation also does not match kernel semantics. Details and suggested changes follow.

### Fresh ISO installs on the target models stop at hardware setup

Hardware setup runs inside the installer's arch-chroot, where `uname -r` is the live ISO kernel, not the installed one (the existing `install/hardware/fix-synaptic-touchpad.sh` notes the same constraint). The driver's `dkms.sh` runs `dkms install -m macbook12-audio-driver -v 0.1 --force` without `-k`, so DKMS targets the live ISO kernel, whose headers are not in the target system. The `omarchy-iso` build notes also describe the install as offline, which the `git clone` and the kernel.org source download both need.

```text
fix-macbook12-audio.sh      git clone / dkms install fails, exits non-zero
  -> run_logged             bash -eE, returns the failure
  -> omarchy-apply-hardware / omarchy-apply-system   set -euo pipefail, exit
  -> ISO finalization step fails -> installation stops
```

**Impact:** before this PR these machines install with silent speakers; with it, a fresh install on MacBook9,1 / MacBook10,1 fails. This follows from the installer and DKMS sources and was reproduced with stubbed commands in a sandbox, not with a real ISO install.

**Suggested change:** do not build the driver in the installer chroot. Defer it to the installed system (for example first boot or a migration), or build only with explicit `-k` for the installed kernel when its headers and network are available, and never let this step fail the install. Apply the chime, soft-mixer and sleep changes only once the driver is installed for the kernel that will boot.

### The DKMS "already installed" check accepts failed and wrong-kernel builds

Both scripts skip the driver when `dkms status | grep -q macbook12-audio` matches. DKMS registers the module ("added") before building and does not remove it when the build fails, and the pattern also matches a build for a different kernel.

```text
migration run 1   DKMS adds module, build fails        -> exits non-zero, retried later
dkms status       macbook12-audio-driver/0.1: added
migration run 2   guard matches -> installer skipped
                  soft-mixer, chime, sleep drop-in written, reboot-required set
                  -> exits 0, marked complete; driver never built
```
(Sandboxed run with a stubbed DKMS failing after "add".)

The same guard hides a kernel upgrade in the same `omarchy update`: packages are upgraded before migrations run, so the Arch DKMS hook has already run for the new kernel before the driver source exists. The migration then builds for `uname -r`, the old kernel. After the requested reboot the new kernel has no module, and the guard still matches on later runs.

**Impact:** speakers can stay silent while the migration is recorded as complete, with no retry.

**Suggested change:** build for each installed kernel with `-k` (for example every `/usr/lib/modules/*/build`), and check per kernel for the installed state, for example `dkms status -m macbook12-audio-driver -v 0.1 -k "$kver"` matching `: installed`.

### The clone in `/usr/src` is picked up as a second DKMS module

The Arch dkms package hook scans `/usr/src/*-*/dkms.conf` and splits the directory name at the last hyphen. The driver's installer copies its source to `/usr/src/macbook12-audio-driver-0.1`, but the git clone stays at `/usr/src/macbook12-audio-driver`:

```text
/usr/src/macbook12-audio-driver-0.1/dkms.conf  ->  macbook12-audio-driver/0.1   (intended)
/usr/src/macbook12-audio-driver/dkms.conf      ->  macbook12-audio/driver       (the clone)
```

DKMS 3.4.3 does not compare `PACKAGE_NAME` in `dkms.conf` with the directory name, so the hook treats the clone as its own module.

**Impact:** on each kernel or header update the hook also tries `dkms install macbook12-audio/driver`, building from the mutable clone and targeting the same `.ko` as the intended module. Which build ends up installed was not tested. The phantom registration also satisfies the `grep -q macbook12-audio` guard above.

**Suggested change:** clone into a temporary directory outside `/usr/src` and remove it once the installer has copied its files, or package the driver.

### Unpinned third-party code runs as root

The scripts clone the driver's default branch (or `git pull` an existing clone) and run its installer as root. Every DKMS build for a new kernel also downloads the matching kernel source from kernel.org.

**Impact:** each install runs whatever the upstream default branch contains at that moment, as root, and each new-kernel build depends on reaching kernel.org.

**Suggested change:** pin a reviewed commit (and verify it after cloning), or take up the packaging option mentioned in the PR description, which also lets the Arch hook build for every installed kernel.

### Suspend explanation: `freeze` and `s2idle` are the same kernel state

In Linux 7.2, `freeze` in `/sys/power/state` and `s2idle` in `/sys/power/mem_sleep` both select `PM_SUSPEND_TO_IDLE`. `/sys/power/mem_sleep` only accepts `s2idle`, `shallow` and `deep`, so it rejects the string `freeze` whether or not S3 exists. With `SuspendState=freeze`, systemd writes `freeze` directly and never uses `mem_sleep`, so `MemorySleepMode=` is not needed.

**Impact:** the code comments, the migration and the PR description state a mechanism the kernel does not have. If these models default to `deep` (S3), the drop-in moves them to suspend-to-idle, which would explain the audio result but may raise battery drain while suspended. That was not tested.

**Suggested change:** check `cat /sys/power/mem_sleep` on an unmodified machine, correct the comments and description accordingly, drop `MemorySleepMode=`, and mention any battery tradeoff in the manual.

**EFI chime write (conditional):** the scripts write a fixed buffer `07 00 00 00 <byte & 0x7f>`. efivarfs takes the first four bytes as the new attribute word and the rest as the complete new payload. Third-party sources (OpenCore, ArchWiki) describe this variable as a 1-byte payload with attributes `0x07`, so the write likely matches, but the layout on these firmware versions is not verified. If it differs, trailing bytes are dropped, or the firmware may reject the attribute change, which would fail the install step or block the migration queue. Writing `data[:4] + bytes([data[4] & 0x7f]) + data[5:]`, or refusing when the length is not 5, avoids both. Separately, the common ArchWiki mute recipe stores `0x80`; clearing bit 7 leaves `0x00` (volume 0), and whether the firmware then powers the amp was not established.

**Optional test improvement:** `test/shell.d/macbook12-audio-test.sh` contains only `grep` checks. It fails on the base only because the new script is absent, and passes at the head with all of the issues above present. Running the migration with stubbed `dkms`/`git` (as `xps13-sidecar-amps-test.sh` does for its script) and a DKMS build that fails after "add" would have caught the second finding.
